segments.text: Published bright-end ultraviolet luminosity functions exist. But can a reader reconstruct their evolution from the frozen two-channel VizieR manifest, rather than from figures alone?

In that manifest, a completed column-name search reaches twenty of one hundred twelve candidate tables. Physical-meaning metadata, encoded as UCD tags, identifies the other ninety-two. Search reach is not eligibility, and other repositories were not exhaustively searched.

Search reach is not eligibility. Of sixty-seven counted catalogues, twenty-seven contribute rows in the frozen slices and forty contribute none. Thirty-four candidates are disqualified, one remains pending, and ten lack a usable magnitude-redshift pair. The contributing catalogues retain six thousand four hundred seventeen raw rows.

Now keep the half-open slice from redshift ten up to, but not including, eleven point five. Every dot is one frozen row with a catalogued ultraviolet-like absolute magnitude. Four hundred twenty of the four hundred fifty-three rows come from the COSMOS2025 LePhare table.

The slice contains four hundred fifty-three raw rows. One hundred seventy-six pass the reported magnitude cut at minus twenty. These catalogued bands are not homogenized to a common rest wavelength, and one hundred sixty-one of the bright rows come from the dominant table.

This census is not a luminosity-function measurement. In the predefined roster, no published-luminosity-function table met the machine-readable data requirements for this slice. That means missing extractable data—not zero galaxies or zero published luminosity functions. No completeness correction or density inference follows.

Human review cleared this study for a Lab landing, not as a journal-refereed, independently validated result. The repair is procedural: publish the luminosity-function values and uncertainties, bin geometry, redshift support, units, Hubble-scaling conventions, and transformations.
